title: Ding-Ding! The Rolling Coin
summary: The Baal Shem Tov and Meir ride a wagon to the town of Brody with completely empty pockets. A kind man gives the rabbi one gold coin, and the rabbi gives it away at once to the house of study and the poor. Meir is alarmed, but surprising things happen on the way, and the little coin rolls from hand to hand... and maybe even comes back. A rhyming story about giving with joy, based on a tale from "In Praise of the Baal Shem Tov."
pages:
A long, long road, and skies of blue,
a little wagon, a horse with bells too.
"Climb up, Meir, and sit by me,
we're off to Brody, you and me!"

In Brody they stopped by an inn for the night,
and Meir checked every pocket, left and right.
And the rabbi's pocket? Not a penny in sight!
Meir sighed, "And my wallet? Left at home on the bed, not right!"

Along came a kind man in a hat of fur,
he held out his hand... and what was there? What was there, sir?
A gold coin! Round, with a little dent on the side.
"This is for you, Rabbi," he said. "One coin," he replied.

The rabbi didn't put it in his pocket or his pack:
"Take it quick to the old house of study, and don't look back!"
Ding-ding! Rolls the coin once more,
from hand to hand, one, two, three, four!

And what was left? For the hungry and poor,
for warm bread and red apples galore.
And one poor man in a patched-up hat
bit his bread and sang, "La-la-la!" just like that.

Meir was alarmed: "Rabbi, what have you done?
Now we have nothing, for the road or for home, not one!"
The rabbi laughed: "Meir, don't worry, don't cry,
the Holy One, blessed be He, is with us all the long way by."

In the town of Radvil, who's coming? Who's here?
A mother with a baby: "Rabbi, a blessing, please, dear!"
And a grandpa with a hen that wouldn't lay,
the rabbi blessed it, and plop! A big egg right away!

Then they brought thanks: eggs, honey and bread,
and coins... and more coins... like rain overhead!
Ding-ding! Rolls the coin once more,
from hand to hand, one, two, three, four!

A little boy with his kippah to one side
held out one coin to the rabbi with pride.
Round and golden, with a little dent in the corner, see...
"That's it!" shouted Meir. "It's back! It came back to me!"

A long, long road, and skies of blue,
and the rabbi gives a coin to a poor man on the path, too.
Ding-ding! Rolls the coin once more,
from hand to hand, one, two, three, four!
